Maintaining Organization: Autonolas DAO (originated from Fetch.ai / Valory ecosystem)
One-Line Description: Open protocol for deploying, coordinating, and economically sustaining autonomous agents that execute on-chain actions
Primary Use Case: Autonomous services coordinating off-chain reasoning with on-chain execution
Target Users: Protocol teams, DAOs, agent developers, infrastructure builders
Ethereum Role: Control Plane; Settlement Layer; Economic Enforcement
Chains Supported: Ethereum L1; Ethereum L2s (e.g., Gnosis Chain)
On-Chain Execution Scope: Smart contract calls; payments; governance execution; service coordination
Off-Chain Compute Location: Hybrid (cloud-based agent compute with optional decentralized components)
Inference / Planning Method: Off-chain agent logic (rule-based and model-assisted) coordinated via on-chain registries
State Persistence Model: Hybrid (off-chain agent memory + on-chain registries, staking, coordination state)
Verification Model: Hybrid (economic guarantees + on-chain transparency; no full zk verification)
Auditability of Agent Actions: High (on-chain actions fully auditable; off-chain logic inspectable)
Failure Handling Mechanism: Service replacement; staking penalties; governance intervention
Permissioning Model: Role-based via on-chain registries and staking
Fee / Incentive Model: OLAS token incentives; service fees; staking rewards
Value Accrual Vector: Network adoption; autonomous service usage; coordination layer effects
Key External Dependencies: Off-chain compute providers; Ethereum infrastructure; optional AI tooling
Primary Risk Factors: Off-chain execution trust; agent misconfiguration; governance capture
Defensibility Source: Network effects; coordination layer; economic incentives
Practitioner’s Note: One of the clearest examples of agent-native infrastructure using Ethereum as a coordination and settlement layer
Practitioner Validation Check: Agents can autonomously execute on Ethereum without human initiation; Ethereum governs permissions and economics

One-Line Description: Decentralized platform for deploying autonomous economic agents that coordinate services and transactions
Primary Use Case: Autonomous agent-based services and machine-to-machine coordination
Inference / Planning Method: Off-chain agent logic with network coordination
State Persistence Model: Hybrid (agent memory off-chain; coordination state on-chain)
Practitioner’s Note: Fetch.ai is broader than Ethereum-first agents but feeds directly into Autonolas/OLAS for Ethereum-native coordination
Practitioner Validation Check: Agents can act autonomously but Ethereum is not always the primary control plane

One-Line Description: Core development team behind open-source autonomous agent frameworks and services
Primary Use Case: Designing, building, and maintaining autonomous agent systems
On-Chain Execution Scope: Smart contract interaction via deployed agents
Practitioner’s Note: Valory is best viewed as the agent R&D and implementation arm of the Autonolas ecosystem
Practitioner Validation Check: Agents deployed by Valory satisfy autonomous on-chain execution criteria

One-Line Description: Economic coordination layer for autonomous services, agents, and operators
Primary Use Case: Incentivizing and sustaining autonomous agent services
Practitioner’s Note: OLAS is not an agent itself but the economic backbone enabling autonomous agent ecosystems
Practitioner Validation Check: Validates inclusion by enforcing autonomous execution economics on Ethereum

One-Line Description: Decentralized network where agent-like systems compete, coordinate, and are economically rewarded, with certain subnets enabling autonomous agents that can trigger on-chain actions
Primary Use Case: Autonomous and semi-autonomous agent intelligence coordinated via incentive-driven subnets
Target Users: ML researchers, agent developers, infra builders
On-Chain Execution Scope: Conditional (agent outputs may trigger Ethereum txs via integrations)
Inference / Planning Method: Model-based inference scored via peer evaluation
State Persistence Model: Primarily off-chain state; optional on-chain anchoring
Sector Adjacency Risk: Include only agent-focused subnets; not all Bittensor activity qualifies
Practitioner’s Note: Valid only where agents can autonomously influence or execute Ethereum-anchored outcomes

One-Line Description: Decentralized automation network enabling autonomous execution of predefined smart-contract actions
Primary Use Case: Autonomous task execution, protocol ops, and conditional on-chain actions
On-Chain Execution Scope: Contract calls; protocol maintenance; execution triggers
Sector Adjacency Risk: Qualifies as an agent executor, not a reasoning agent
Practitioner’s Note: Passes only when used for autonomous, self-triggering execution

One-Line Description: Decentralized network coordinating autonomous on-chain tasks via economically incentivized keepers
Primary Use Case: Autonomous protocol maintenance and execution tasks
Practitioner’s Note: Early form of autonomous agents; limited intelligence
Practitioner Validation Check: Autonomous execution without human initiation is clearly satisfied

One-Line Description: Secure operations platform enabling autonomous execution, monitoring, and response actions for smart contracts
Primary Use Case: Autonomous contract operations, emergency response, and protocol maintenance
On-Chain Execution Scope: Contract calls; upgrades; pausing; operational tasks
Composable With: AI Agents; DeFi Ops; RWAs (ops layer)
Practitioner’s Note: Qualifies only when Defender automations execute without human approval
Practitioner Validation Check: Passes inclusion when used for autonomous, policy-enforced execution

One-Line Description: Decentralized automation network enabling autonomous, condition-based execution of smart contract functions
Primary Use Case: Autonomous upkeep, protocol maintenance, and agent-triggered execution
On-Chain Execution Scope: Contract calls; state updates; maintenance actions
Practitioner’s Note: Included only where Automation acts as an autonomous agent executor
Practitioner Validation Check: Autonomous on-chain execution without human initiation is clearly satisfied

One-Line Description: Autonomous agents embedded in DAOs that manage treasury assets, rebalance positions, and execute financial policies without human initiation
Primary Use Case: Treasury rebalancing, yield deployment, asset diversification
Practitioner’s Note: These agents replace human treasury committees, not dashboards
Practitioner Validation Check: Agent must move funds autonomously under pre-approved policies

One-Line Description: Autonomous agents that execute governance decisions automatically once proposals pass
Primary Use Case: Proposal execution; parameter updates; contract actions
Practitioner’s Note: These agents eliminate manual multisig execution risk

One-Line Description: Autonomous agents that manage liquidity, pricing, or rebalancing in on-chain markets

One-Line Description: Autonomous agents that monitor positions and execute liquidations or risk interventions

Practitioner’s Note: These are the earliest true autonomous agents in DeFi
Practitioner Validation Check: Autonomous execution on threshold breach is sufficient

Practitioner’s Note: Critical for high-stakes autonomous agents

One-Line Description: Verifiable AI compute infrastructure enabling auditability and reproducibility of agent inference

Practitioner’s Note: Focuses on compute correctness, not agents themselves

One-Line Description: zkML tooling enabling provable AI inference and agent reasoning
Primary Use Case: Cryptographically provable agent decisions
Practitioner’s Note: Suitable for regulatory-sensitive agent use cases

One-Line Description: zkVM enabling general-purpose verifiable computation usable by autonomous agents

One-Line Description: Verifiable computation framework enabling trustless data and computation proofs for smart contracts and agents

One-Line Description: Autonomous agent systems that compete or coordinate to capture MEV, optimize execution, and manage transaction ordering
